discovery: Invention of the quantum cascade laser
motivation: In 1994 Faist, Capasso and co-workers at Bell Labs demonstrated the quantum cascade laser, building on Cho's molecular beam epitaxy. It was a new kind of light source: its emission wavelength is set by quantum engineering of the band structure, not by the material's band gap. Electrons cascade through designed intersubband transitions, so one device can cover the mid-infrared through the terahertz range, where molecules show their vibrational fingerprints. Until then that range lacked compact, powerful, tunable coherent sources. QCLs, and the QCL frequency combs that followed, now support trace-gas sensing, environmental monitoring, industrial and security spectroscopy, astronomy and emerging medical diagnostics from breath and body fluids. This is a model example of band-structure engineering at the quantum level becoming a disruptive technology. It opened a whole spectral window to precise observation and has brought wide benefit to society.
